title: The Teenager Who Conquered the WTA Finals
summary: Mirra Andreeva arrived at the WTA Finals so nervous that she had what she called a little breakdown in a practice session before the tournament. She left California as the champion. The 19-year-old French Open winner beat Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final at Indian Wells, becoming the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The last teenager to do it was a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004. Andreeva did not drop a set all week and lost only 26 games across her five matches. She has now risen to second in the world rankings and will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina. What made the week even more remarkable is that Andreeva had won only one of her six matches against top-10 players in 2026 before the tournament. She beat three of them on her way to the title, including a demolition of four-time major champion Aryna Sabalenka. Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the tour, she lost her serve lead three times across the two sets. Each time she reset, attacked with her backhand and put the pressure back on. After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, she marched back to her chair, then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front. Andreeva said her fighting mindset helped her to be more brave and aggressive in the important moments. She called the whole week just a dream. Just as she did when she won the French Open, she ended her victory speech by thanking herself, a twist on a quote she borrowed from rapper Snoop Dogg. From a pre-tournament wobble to the youngest champion in more than two decades, Andreeva's week in California was a masterclass in bouncing back.
why_it_matters: Andreeva shows that even teenagers can beat the world's best when they stay brave under pressure.
